name: University of Glasgow

settingEvidence.evidence: University of Glasgow main campus, located in the West End of Glasgow.

fees.text: £9,790 a year for students from England, Wales and Northern Ireland starting in 2026/27. Glasgow's 2027/28 fee is still shown as 'TBC', and Glasgow says these students' fees rise each year of study in line with the UK Government's tuition fee cap.

source.evidence: Tuition fees 2026/27 | Tuition fees for students from England, Wales and Northern Ireland | Cost per year | Standard cost | £9,790

livingCosts.text: University halls cost about £130 to £239 a week in 2026/27: shared rooms from £129.92, single rooms from £168, ensuite singles about £209.51 and studios up to £239.40. Rent includes heating, utilities, Wi-Fi and contents insurance. Most contracts run from 11 September 2026 to 11 June 2027.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 24 October 2026, 9am to 3pm on the Glasgow campus. No later open days are listed yet.

source.evidence: Saturday 24 October, 9am - 3pm

contextual.summary: Glasgow's lower 'adjusted' offers are only for applicants living in Scotland. Students from England, Wales or Northern Ireland can only get a possible adjusted offer by completing Glasgow's Sutton Trust Summer School, and Glasgow does not publish the A-level grades.
contextual.rulesText: Glasgow says it operates contextualised admissions for applicants living in Scotland. The groups it lists for guaranteed adjusted offers are people living in a Scottish postcode area in SIMD deciles 1-4 (MD20/40), people with care experience, estranged from family, carers, people seeking asylum and people with refugee status. Adjusted grades are published for Scottish Highers only, not A-levels. Completing a Glasgow pre-entry programme (including the Sutton Trust Summer School) 'may lead to' an adjusted offer.

source.evidence: we operate a system of contextualised admissions for applicants living in Scotland.

notes: Scottish university: these degrees are 4 years (Honours in years 3 and 4) and years 1 and 2 also include other subjects. Glasgow's degree pages are for entry in 2027; no 2028 pages yet (checked 2026-10-21), so all courses use 2027 entry.

Glasgow's degree pages fill in the A-level entry requirements with a degree picker and a country picker. This record uses the England selection for every course (Wales and Northern Ireland show the same A-level requirements for Economics).

Standard A-level offer is AAB for every course recorded. Glasgow's published widening-access (adjusted) offers are for Scottish Highers and applicants living in Scotland, so no lower A-level offer is recorded.

The only route to an adjusted offer for Year 12 students from England, Wales or Northern Ireland is the Sutton Trust Summer School hosted at Glasgow (recorded in each course's alternative offers). Glasgow's own Top-Up, Reach, Access to a Career, Taster Week and WP Summer School programmes are for pupils in Scotland, SIMD postcode areas or school leavers holding an adjusted offer, so none is listed as a programme.
No admissions test: Glasgow is not on UAT-UK's TMUA list for 2027 entry and none is listed in the entry requirements shown for these courses.

Glasgow RUK Access Bursary (2027-28 entry): £2,500 a year if household income is under £25,001, £1,500 a year if between £25,000 and £35,000. RUK Excellence Scholarship: £3,000 for the first year for A*AA or better at A-level in one sitting (fees page).

Other economics joint degrees on Glasgow's Economics page (not recorded as separate courses, England selection): Economics/Business & Management LN12 (AAB, English or Humanities, Mathematics), Economics/Accountancy BAcc LN14 (AAB, Mathematics at A, English or Humanities, GCSE English B or 5/6), Mathematics/Economics BSc LG1D and Economics/Statistics BSc GL31 (AAB, Mathematics at A), Economics/Philosophy LVC5 (as Economics).

Postcode is the Adam Smith Building, 2 Discovery Place, home of the Adam Smith Business School that runs these degrees; Glasgow says its main entrance faces the main University campus and Kelvingrove Park. The degree pages say the courses are taught at the Gilmorehill campus.
